title: Upstream P0211 — incremental_simulator
source_prompt:
Gameplay Loop:
You are building a grid-based incremental game called "Mushroom Manager". In Mushroom Manager, players are given a 8x8 grid that they place mushrooms onto. The goal of Mushroom Manager is to gain spores, a currency generated by placed mushrooms every second. There are 5 mushroom variations: Basic Shrooms generate 1 spore per second, Fever Shrooms make adjacent mushrooms generate 2x spores (effect can stack), Radio Shrooms increase the range of mushrooms with AoE effects like fever shrooms or other radio shrooms, Shy Shrooms generate 10 spores per second but generate none if adjacent to another mushroom, and Pop Shrooms generate 1 spore per second but when popped they active the pop effect 10 times instead of once. Every second, any placed mushroom has a 10% chance to become "poppable", highlighting it in yellow. Poppable shrooms can be clicked to immediately generate it's current spore amount * 10. Each mushroom type has a base cost of 10 spores, but placing the mushroom then makes the next mushroom of the same type cost 2x as much.

UI/UX: The game supports 8 players at a time, with claimable plots. Players are assigned a plot automatically upon joining. The plots contain the 8x8 playing grid, which is a green checkerboard of 4x4x4 grass material blocks. Players will see their name and avatar on a billboard in front of their plot. The shroom inventory is accessed at the bottom of the screen, displaying all mushroom types. Players can press a mushroom to select it, and then click on a grid part to place it. Alternatively, they can drag from the button and onto the grid to place it. Mushroom buttons display their current cost. If a player right clicks a mushroom (or long presses on mobile), that mushroom is deleted and the cost for that mushroom type is cut in half.

Aesthetics:
The game uses a classic, blocky Roblox aesthetic. Basic mushrooms are blue and plain. Fever shrooms are red and themed around fire. Radio Shrooms look like a satellite dish. Shy Shrooms are normal sized when active, but tiny when inactive. Pop Shrooms look like they have additional heads coming out of the main head. When Mushrooms are active on the grid, they grow and shrink in size slightly for a bouncy effect.Shrooms display how many spores they're generating over their mesh when the mouse hovers over it or the player is nearby. Popping a shroom causes the shroom to briefly grow in size with an elastic like effect, before springing back to size. Poppable shrooms are highlighted when poppable. Throughout the game, it is a priority to include fun vfx and sfx for every interaction. Interactions with UI, shrooms, etc. must always have vfx/sfx for actions such as hover, click, etc. when relevant.

title: Upstream P0212 — incremental_simulator
source_prompt:
Game Design Doc - "Aether Roll" (3D RNG Aura Collector)
Target platform: Roblox (Luau). Rendering: Fully 3D world with a third-person camera. This is NOT a 2D or GUI-only game - the player controls an avatar walking through explorable 3D biomes. UI overlays sit on top of the 3D world.
Genre: Incremental / RNG collector, inspired by Sol's RNG and similar "rolling" games. Core loop is roll → collect rare auras → boost luck → chase rarer auras.

1. Core Concept
The player controls a 3D avatar in an explorable world. They press a Roll button to generate a random cosmetic Aura (a particle/visual effect attached to their character) drawn from a weighted rarity table. Rarer auras are astronomically unlikely. The player increases their Luck stat over time (via gear, potions, quests, and biomes) to improve odds, and collects auras in an inventory. There is no combat requirement to progress - the chase itself is the game.
Auras are purely cosmetic and confer no combat power; their value is rarity and appearance. This is intentional and central to the design.

2. The 3D World
The world is a single explorable place composed of connected zones. Build it in 3D with real Parts/terrain, not menus.
 • Spawn Hub - central area where the player begins. Contains the roll station platform, NPC vendors, and paths to other zones.
 • Biomes - distinct 3D environments the world cycles through (see §6). Each has its own skybox, lighting, terrain, ambient audio, and particle weather. Biomes change globally on a timer for all players in the server.
 • Crafting area - a building/room containing the crafting workbench NPC.
 • Explorable paths - walkable terrain connecting zones, with collectible nodes scattered around (materials for crafting).
The avatar is standard Roblox R15. The equipped aura renders as attached ParticleEmitters / Beams / Trails and dynamic lighting on the character, visible in the 3D world to all players.

3. Core Loop
 1 Player walks avatar to (or is anywhere near) the roll station.
 2 Player presses Roll (button on screen, or auto-roll toggle).
 3 A short 3D roll animation plays (character glows, effect builds).
 4 Server computes the result from the weighted table using current Luck.
 5 Result aura is revealed with a reveal effect scaled to rarity (screen shake, sound sting, server-wide announcement for top-tier rolls).
 6 Aura is added to inventory; player may equip it.
 7 Player spends downtime raising Luck (potions, gear, quests, moving to favorable biomes), then rolls again.
Roll speed is a stat. Base cooldown ~1s; gear and gamepasses reduce it. Auto-roll repeatedly rolls on cooldown while the player is AFK.

4. Rarity & Luck System (server-authoritative)
All RNG must run on the server. The client only requests a roll and displays the result. Never trust client-reported results.
Rarity tiers
Use a tiered table. Each aura has a base "1 in N" chance. Suggested tier bands (tune later):
Tier
Base odds range
Example count
Common
1 in 2 - 1 in 10
many
Uncommon
1 in 10 - 1 in 100
many
Rare
1 in 100 - 1 in 1,000
~20
Epic
1 in 1k - 1 in 10k
~15
Legendary
1 in 10k - 1 in 1M
~10
Mythic
1 in 1M - 1 in 100M
~6
Transcendent
1 in 100M - 1 in 3B
~5
Event / Craft-only
separate pools
varies
Luck calculation
Store each aura as a base weight (higher weight = more common). Luck reduces the effective threshold for rare auras. A workable model:
Luck = ((1 + BaseLuck) * RollMultiplier + SpecialLuck) * VIPMultiplier
Rolling algorithm (list-search style, matching the genre):
 1 Build the roll pool of all auras available in the current biome/event.
 2 Sort candidates from rarest to most common.
 3 For each candidate, effective chance = baseChance / Luck (higher Luck → rarer things become attainable).
 4 Roll a random number per candidate in rarity order; first one that "hits" is awarded. If none hit, award a common fallback.
Luck sources stack: equipped gear (glove/device), active potions (multiplicative), biome multipliers (biome-exclusive auras and discounts), VIP gamepass, and a "every Nth roll gives 2x luck" pity mechanic for early-game feel.
Keep a config table (ModuleScript) of all auras: {id, name, tier, baseChance, biomeExclusive?, craftOnly?, vfxConfig} so content is data-driven and easy to extend.

5. Auras (cosmetic rewards)
Each aura is a visual effect package applied to the avatar in 3D:
 • ParticleEmitters (color, texture, rate, size over lifetime)
 • Optional PointLight / colored character glow
 • Optional Trail/Beam
 • Optional custom sound loop while equipped
 • Rarer auras = more elaborate, multi-layered effects and unique colors.
Player can equip one aura at a time (or allow a small loadout later). Equipped aura is replicated so other players see it. Inventory stores counts of each rolled aura.
Start with ~40-60 auras across tiers for launch; the data-driven table makes adding more trivial.

6. Biomes
Biomes are timed global world-states affecting the 3D environment and the roll pool.
 • The server picks the active biome on a schedule (e.g., rotate every 5-10 min, with rare biomes on low probability).
 • Each biome: changes Lighting (ClockTime, ambient, fog), skybox, weather particles, and applies a luck/roll modifier plus unlocks biome-exclusive auras.
 • Announce biome changes server-wide with an on-screen banner and sound.
 • Examples: Normal, Windy (minor luck boost), Rainy, Snowy, Starfall (rare, big luck boost + exclusive auras), Corruption/Null (very rare, exclusive high-tier auras).
Biome transitions should animate (lighting tween, particles fade in) rather than snap.

7. Crafting
At a 3D workbench NPC, players convert collected auras + materials into gear/potions or craft-only auras (guaranteed top-tier route bypassing pure RNG).
 • Gear (gloves/devices): permanent Luck and/or roll-speed boosts while equipped. Higher recipes = bigger boosts.
 • Potions: temporary Luck multipliers (timed buffs); consumed on use, stack multiplicatively.
 • Craft-only auras: require multiple rare ingredients; a guaranteed path to a prestige aura.
 • Wildcard ingredient (optional): substitutes for a missing recipe component.
Recipes are data-driven config. Crafting UI is a screen overlay opened by interacting with the workbench in 3D.

8. Progression Systems
 • Quests - an NPC gives objectives ("roll 100 times", "collect a Rare aura", "visit the Starfall biome"). Rewards: coins, potions, materials. Data-driven quest table.
 • Currency (Coins) - earned from quests/achievements; spent at shop NPCs on gear, potions, storage upgrades.
 • Inventory storage - upgradable cap on how many auras can be stored.
 • Achievements - milestone rewards (roll counts, rarity firsts) granting coins.
 • (Optional) Prestige - reset progress for permanent luck bonuses to enable long-term retention.
 • Monetization (optional gamepasses): Auto-Roll, Quick-Roll (skip animation), VIP luck multiplier, 2x luck. Keep purely convenience/cosmetic; no pay-to-win over other players since auras are cosmetic.

9. Data Persistence
 • Use DataStoreService (with a session-locking wrapper such as ProfileService/ProfileStore pattern) to persist: owned auras + counts, equipped aura, coins, gear owned/equipped, active potions, quest progress, achievements, storage level, prestige level.
 • Save on leave and on periodic autosave. Handle DataStore failures gracefully (retry, don't wipe).
 • Never store or trust roll results client-side.

10. Client / Server Architecture
 • Server (ServerScriptService): all RNG, luck math, inventory writes, crafting validation, quest completion, currency, biome scheduling, DataStore. Expose a small set of RemoteEvents/RemoteFunctions: RequestRoll, EquipAura, Craft, BuyItem, UsePotion, CompleteQuest.
 • Client (StarterPlayerScripts): input handling, camera, UI overlays, playing roll/reveal VFX and equipped-aura visuals, auto-roll loop that calls RequestRoll.
 • Shared (ReplicatedStorage): config ModuleScripts (aura table, biome table, recipe table, quest table) and enums so client and server agree on data.
 • Anti-exploit: validate every remote (cooldowns, ownership, currency checks) server-side; rate-limit RequestRoll.

11. UI (overlay on the 3D world)
Screen-space GUI on top of the 3D game:
 • Roll button + auto-roll toggle + current Luck readout + roll cooldown.
 • Inventory panel (grid of owned auras, equip button, rarity color coding).
 • Crafting panel, Shop panel, Quest tracker.
 • Active-biome banner and buff indicators.
 • Rare-roll celebration overlay + server-wide announcement feed.
UI must not replace the 3D world - the avatar and biome remain visible behind panels.

12. Build Order (suggested milestones for the agent)
 1 3D hub place with spawn, roll station, walkable avatar, third-person camera.
 2 Server-side roll system + shared aura config (start with ~10 auras across tiers) + basic reveal.
 3 Equipping auras with 3D VFX replicated to all players.
 4 Inventory + DataStore persistence.
 5 Luck stat + gear/potions + luck math.
 6 Biomes (lighting/skybox/weather + roll-pool modifiers + scheduler).
 7 Crafting workbench + recipes.
 8 Quests, currency, shop, achievements.
 9 Auto-roll, gamepasses, polish (sounds, screen shake, announcements).
 10 Balance pass on the rarity table and luck curve.

13. Key Reminders
 • It is a 3D game. Real explorable environment, third-person avatar, replicated aura VFX - not a menu simulator.
 • Auras are cosmetic only; rarity is the reward.
 • All randomness and economy logic is server-authoritative.
 • Content (auras, biomes, recipes, quests) is data-driven via config modules for easy expansion.

source_prompt:
# Piggy Chomp

Create a fun, colorful 3D game for young kids called Piggy Chomp.

## Core Gameplay
- The game lasts 60 seconds.
- A friendly cartoon crocodile runs around the edge of a small lake.
- The player stands in one spot with a giant slingshot.
- The player drags back the slingshot and launches cute pink piggies.
- If a piggy hits the crocodile:
 - The crocodile makes a funny surprised animation.
 - A cheerful sound plays.
 - The player earns 1 point.
 - The crocodile keeps running.

## Controls
- Drag to aim.
- Release to launch.
- Show a simple aiming arc while dragging.
- Automatically give the player another piggy after every shot.

## Timer
- Show a large 60-second countdown at the top.
- When time reaches zero:
 - Stop gameplay.
 - Show the final score.
 - Show any new badge unlocked.
 - Display a Play Again button.

## Animal Badge Collection
Every successful crocodile hit grants one random animal badge.

Examples:
- Unicorn
- Panda
- Tiger
- Elephant
- Penguin
- Fox
- Bunny
- Koala
- Giraffe
- Dolphin
- Owl
- Dragon
- Lion
- Bear
- Monkey
- Turtle
- Flamingo
- Red Panda
- Hedgehog
- Sloth

Rules:
- Only unlock badges the player does not already own.
- Save unlocked badges permanently.
- Add a Badge Library button on the main menu.
- The Badge Library displays every badge.
- Locked badges appear as dark silhouettes with question marks.
- Unlocked badges are colorful and can be tapped to view larger.

## Main Menu
Create three large buttons:
- ▶ Play
- 🏅 Badge Library
- ⚙️ Settings

## Art Style
- Bright, colorful, playful.
- Rounded shapes.
- Big smiling characters.
- No violence or scary effects.
- Kid-friendly animations and sounds.

## Progression
The main goal is:
1. Play a 60-second round.
2. Hit the crocodile as many times as possible.
3. Unlock new animal badges.
4. Collect every badge in the Badge Library.
5. Play again to complete the collection.

## Saving
Save permanently:
- Highest score.
- Total crocodile hits.
- All unlocked badges.

Focus on making the controls smooth, satisfying, and fun for children ages 4-8.

title: Upstream P0246 — minigame
source_prompt:
Build a round-based multiplayer Roblox game called DOORBELL DASH.

=== ONE-SENTENCE PITCH ===
You ring doorbells on an impossibly tall suburban house. Every door hides a
different outcome. Get paid, get trapped, or get chased down the street by a
furious resident in a bathrobe.

=== CORE LOOP (must feel good within 5 seconds of spawning) ===
1. Walk up to any door on the house.
2. Press E (or tap the prompt) to ring the doorbell.
3. The door rolls a hidden outcome and reacts instantly.
4. Rewards drop as physical glowing coins you must physically touch to pick up.
5. Coins in your pocket are UNBANKED. Run back to the mailbox at the street
 and deposit them to make them permanent.
6. Repeat. Ring faster, ring riskier, bank before you lose it.

The tension is entirely: "one more door before I bank."

=== DOOR OUTCOME TABLE ===
Each door re-rolls its hidden outcome every 20 seconds. Base odds:

 45% PAYOUT - coins spill out, small to medium
 20% NOTHING - door creaks open on an empty room, sad trombone
 15% RESIDENT - an angry NPC bursts out and chases the ringer
 10% TRAP - door slams a pie / anvil / bucket of paint on you,
 stunning you for 1.5s and dropping 25% of your
 unbanked coins on the ground for anyone to grab
 7% MYSTERY BOX - a wobbling box; touch it for a random buff
 (2x coins for 20s, super speed, ghost mode, magnet)
 3% JACKPOT - the door explodes into a fountain of 200+ coins with a
 loud siren and a screen-wide golden flash. Everyone on
 the server hears it and sees a marker on that door.

=== THE CONTENTION MECHANIC (this is what makes it multiplayer) ===
- HOT DOORS: after any door pays out well, it glows red-hot and its PAYOUT
 odds double for 15 seconds. A floating flame icon marks it server-wide.
 Players will sprint across the map and fight over these. This single rule
 generates all the rivalry - do not cut it.
- Doors go on an 8-second cooldown per player after ringing, but ANY other
 player can ring the same door immediately. First to reach it wins the roll.
- DROPPED COINS ARE PUBLIC. When someone gets trapped or caught, their spilled
 coins are free for anyone. Vultures are a valid playstyle.
- Residents chase the player who rang, but will switch targets if another
 player runs closer to them. Players can and will bait residents into rivals.
- No direct player combat. No weapons. All conflict is positional and comedic.

=== ROUND STRUCTURE ===
Server size: 12 players.

INTERMISSION (30 seconds)
 Players stand in the cul-de-sac. Big flip-clock countdown on the mailbox.
 Upgrade truck is open. Round leaderboard from the previous round is displayed
 on a billboard. Winner of the last round wears a glowing crown.

ROUND (3 minutes)
 House unlocks. All 50 doors go live. Coins are worth 1x for the first minute,
 1.5x in the second, 2x in the final minute - so the last 60 seconds are a
 frantic, greedy scramble where nobody wants to leave to bank.

 Final 10 seconds: "LAST CALL" siren. Any unbanked coins at the buzzer are
 LOST. Watching players sprint for the mailbox is the best moment in the game.

RESULTS (15 seconds)
 Top 3 podium rises out of the lawn. Confetti. XP awarded.

=== LEVEL-UP SYSTEM ===
Persistent account level 1-60. XP = total coins banked, all-time.
Leveling is fast early (level 5 in the first two rounds) and slows gradually.

Each level grants 1 upgrade point. Five upgrade tracks, 12 ranks each,
purchased from the ICE CREAM TRUCK parked in the cul-de-sac:

 LUCK Shifts the outcome table. At max rank: PAYOUT 60%, RESIDENT 8%,
 TRAP 4%, JACKPOT 8%. Never removes risk entirely.
 SPRINT Move speed +2% per rank. Also increases sprint stamina.
 NERVE Reduces trap stun duration and lets you shrug off the first
 resident hit each round.
 POCKETS Increases unbanked coin cap. Low ranks force frequent banking
 trips; high ranks let you gamble huge stacks.
 REACH Ring doorbells from further away, and ring 15% faster per rank.

Show a chunky, sticker-styled upgrade menu with big plus buttons and a
satisfying "ka-chunk" sound on purchase.

MILESTONE UNLOCKS (cosmetic, drives long-term retention):
 Lvl 5 Bathrobe outfit
 Lvl 10 Bicycle (faster, but you can't carry coins while riding)
 Lvl 15 Custom doorbell chime (you choose the sound everyone hears)
 Lvl 25 Glowing footprint trail
 Lvl 40 Pizza delivery uniform - residents hesitate for 1 second
 Lvl 60 Golden thumb - permanent visible aura, a flex

=== LEADERBOARDS ===
1. LIVE ROUND BOARD - right side of screen, always visible, top 5 by banked
 coins this round. Your own row is pinned at the bottom if you're not top 5.
2. THE BILLBOARD - a physical billboard in the cul-de-sac, three tabs:
 - WEEKLY: most coins banked, resets Monday. Top 3 get a crown cosmetic.
 - ALL-TIME DOORBELLS RUNG: a pure volume stat. Absurd numbers. Very sticky.
 - RESIDENTS OUTRUN: bragging-rights stat for chase survivors.
3. Persistent Roblox leaderstats: Level, Banked (all-time), Rung.

=== THE HOUSE - VISUAL DESIGN ===
Setting: a suburban cul-de-sac frozen at golden-hour dusk. Warm orange light,
long purple shadows, a few fireflies, sprinklers hissing on the lawns.

The house is the star and should read as WRONG on first sight: a single
suburban home that has been vertically stacked five stories tall, each floor a
mismatched architectural style - vinyl siding, then brick, then a log cabin,
then stucco, then a slightly-too-formal Victorian top floor with a widow's
walk. It leans very slightly. It is far too tall for its plot.

Its entire front face is a collage of 50 DOORS crammed edge to edge with no
logic - doors at floor level, doors halfway up the wall, doors upside down,
doors behind other doors. Players reach upper doors via exterior wooden
staircases, a fire escape, scaffolding, a trellis, and one very long ladder.

DOOR VARIETY (each door type visually telegraphs its personality):
 screen door, castle drawbridge, refrigerator door, cat flap, bank vault,
 airlock, submarine hatch, saloon swinging doors, revolving door, elevator
 doors, a beaded curtain, a door made entirely of cardboard, one door that
 is clearly just a painting of a door, a doggy door only small avatars fit
 through, a door with 40 locks on it, a door labeled DO NOT.

Art direction: chunky low-poly, heavy saturation, no realism. Palette is mint
green, salmon, mustard yellow, and dusty teal. Everything slightly oversized
and rounded - mailbox is comically huge, the doorbells are the size of dinner
plates. Cartoon squash-and-stretch on every interaction.

VFX: expanding white sound-rings pulse out of a rung doorbell. Coins are fat
spinning discs with a chime. Traps are silent-film slapstick - pies, anvils,
paint buckets, a single enormous boxing glove on a spring.

RESIDENT NPCS: rotund, furious, wearing bathrobes and curlers, wielding
slippers, rolled newspapers, and one with a garden hose. They run with an
exaggerated waddle. They shout muffled gibberish, never real words. When they
give up, they stop, shake a fist, and slam the door.

AUDIO: 50 distinct doorbell chimes - normal ding-dongs, a foghorn, a cow, a
full 8-second orchestral fanfare, one that's just a man saying "hello."
Background: cicadas, distant lawnmower, an ice cream truck jingle looping
faintly. The jackpot siren should be genuinely startling.

UI: thick rounded borders, hand-drawn sticker aesthetic, bouncy tweened
animations on every number change. Coin counter should physically jiggle.

=== MOBILE ===
Design for mobile first. Single large contextual RING button bottom-right,
sprint on the left thumbstick double-tap. Never require more than one finger.

=== MONETIZATION (keep it light) ===
Cosmetic-only outfits and doorbell chimes. One 2x-coins gamepass. A "Skip the
Walk" teleport-to-mailbox consumable. Do not sell Luck.

=== SUCCESS CRITERIA ===
A brand-new player should ring their first doorbell within 8 seconds of
spawning and understand the entire game without reading a word of tutorial.

Their gameplay should reward map knowledge, positioning, and precise movement. The Killer should be a powerful tracking-focused juggernaut capable of locating Survivors through unique tracking abilities, revealing their approximate locations for short periods, and applying constant pressure across the map. In addition to strong close-range attacks, the Killer should possess multiple ranged abilities themed around Undertale and Deltarune-inspired magical attacks, such as projectiles, energy blasts, or summoned hazards, giving Survivors opportunities to dodge while making the Killer feel powerful and threatening. Design both character selection menus and the in-game HUD with a clean, modern style inspired by Undertale and Deltarune aesthetics, featuring smooth animations, readable fonts, subtle pixel-inspired design elements, and consistent visual effects that match the rest of the game's atmosphere.

Mapa: Crea un pueblo abandonado de noche con casas, callejones, una escuela, una iglesia, una estación de servicio, una tienda, una comisaría, un parque, alcantarillas, edificios explorables, múltiples rutas, atajos, ventanas, puertas y escondites. El mapa debe estar optimizado para partidas multijugador.
Roles: Crea dos equipos: Runner y Chaser. Los jugadores son asignados aleatoriamente al comenzar cada ronda.
Runner: Debe ser más ágil, girar más rápido, saltar mejor y moverse con mayor fluidez. Utiliza animaciones del catálogo oficial de Roblox (R15) para caminar, correr, saltar, caer e inactivo. No dejes al personaje sin animaciones.
Chaser: Debe verse más intimidante y tener una habilidad que aumente su velocidad durante 10 segundos, seguida de un tiempo de recarga. Utiliza también animaciones oficiales del catálogo de Roblox para caminar, correr, saltar e inactivo. No dejes al personaje estático.
Panel de administrador: Agrega un panel para pruebas que permita cambiar el rol de cualquier jugador entre Runner y Chaser, iniciar o finalizar rondas, reiniciar la partida y forzar el cambio de roles.
Jugabilidad: Las rondas comienzan desde un lobby interactivo. Los jugadores pueden caminar por el lobby y la partida inicia automáticamente. Durante la partida, los Chasers deben eliminar a los Runners antes de que termine el tiempo. Al finalizar una ronda, los roles pueden cambiar aleatoriamente para la siguiente.
Atmósfera: No agregues música de fondo. Utiliza solo sonidos ambientales como viento, puertas, pasos y luces parpadeantes.
Último minuto: Cuando quede un minuto, el mapa debe volverse mucho más oscuro y los Chasers deben emitir un brillo visible para aumentar la tensión.
Calidad: Utiliza únicamente recursos oficiales de Roblox cuando sea posible. Si no puedes crear animaciones personalizadas, utiliza las animaciones oficiales del catálogo. No dejes personajes sin animaciones. El juego debe ser funcional, organizado y fácil de ampliar con nuevas mecánicas en el futuro.

title: Upstream P0280 — one_vs_all
source_prompt:
Roblox AI Prompt - "RUN" (Prey vs Predators Survival Game)
Copy and paste the prompt below into the Roblox Studio AI Assistant / Creator Hub AI chat.
PROMPT
Create a Roblox survival game called "RUN", a Prey vs Predators experience, similar in spirit to games like "Doors" or "Flee the Facility" but with multiple large maps and a role-swap system. Build it fully in English (all UI text, instructions, and in-game dialogue must be in English).
Core Concept
At the start of each round, players are randomly split into two teams:
Prey (majority of players) - must survive and avoid being caught.
Predators (minority, 1-3 players depending on lobby size) - must hunt down and eliminate the Prey.
Each round has an estimated survival timer (example: 6-8 minutes) displayed on screen (a HUD countdown).
Important rule: when the timer runs out, the round does NOT end. Instead, all players swap roles - Prey become Predators and Predators become Prey - and a new timer starts. The match continues with these swapped roles for another timed segment.
The overall match can consist of multiple role-swap cycles (e.g., 2-3 swaps) before the round fully ends and scores are tallied.
Track a scoring system: Prey earn points for time survived and objectives completed; Predators earn points for eliminations. Total score across all role phases determines the round winner(s).
Maps
Design multiple large, distinct maps with different layouts, hiding spots, chokepoints, and escape routes:
Big School - large school building with classrooms, hallways, gym, cafeteria, rooftop access, and lockers to hide in.
Shopping Mall - multi-floor mall with stores, food court, escalators, parking garage, and security rooms.
Abandoned Neighborhood - outdoor residential area with empty houses, backyards, alleyways, and a small park.
(Optional extra maps) Hospital, Subway Station, Office Building, Summer Camp - each with a unique theme and layout logic.
Each map should support:
Multiple hiding spots (closets, lockers, dumpsters, under furniture).
Sprint/stamina mechanics for Prey.
Chase mechanics and detection radius for Predators.
Environmental hazards or interactive objects (doors that lock, vents, alarms) that can help Prey escape or slow down Predators.
Roles & Mechanics
Prey:
No combat ability, must rely on stealth, speed, and environment use.
Can perform quick tasks/objectives on the map for bonus points (e.g., generators, keycards).
Can be eliminated (caught) by Predators, which removes them from that phase (but they return as Predators in the next swap, or are respawned as spectators/next phase depending on design).
Predators:
Enhanced speed or a special ability (e.g., short detection burst, sprint, or map sense) to hunt Prey.
Limited-use abilities on a cooldown to keep the chase balanced.
Cannot camp in one spot indefinitely - add a mechanic like a shrinking safe zone or periodic "reveal ping" to keep the game moving.
Main Menu
Design a main menu screen that plays when the player first joins the game:
Background scene: a dark forest at night - tall silhouetted trees, thick fog/mist near the ground, dim moonlight filtering through the branches. Very low ambient lighting to create a tense, eerie atmosphere.
Campfire: a lit campfire in the middle of the scene (either as the visual centerpiece behind the UI or in a 3D background behind the menu camera), with flickering flame particles and a warm orange glow that contrasts with the dark surroundings.
Ambient sound: looping night forest ambience - crickets chirping, occasional distant wind, and a soft crackling campfire sound layered in.
Logo: a bold, rough, hand-drawn/sketchy style "RUN" title logo (thick uneven strokes, slightly jagged edges, like it was scratched or drawn in a hurry) - should feel raw and unsettling rather than clean or corporate.
Buttons: two main rounded rectangular buttons below the logo, hand-drawn/sketch style to match the logo:
PLAY - takes the player into matchmaking/lobby.
SETTINGS - opens a settings menu (audio volume, graphics quality, controls/keybinds).
Buttons should have a subtle hover/press animation (slight scale-up or wobble) to match the sketchy, handmade art style of the logo.
UI/UX Requirements
Countdown timer clearly visible at the top of the screen.
Role indicator (Prey/Predator) shown to each player with distinct color coding (e.g., blue for Prey, red for Predator).
End-of-phase announcement: "Roles have switched!" with a short transition/respawn sequence.
Scoreboard accessible mid-game showing points per player.
Additional Notes for the AI
Prioritize balance: adjust Predator count and speed based on total player count.
Make role swaps feel like a natural game beat, not a jarring reset - consider a short cinematic transition or safe countdown before the next phase starts.
Keep matches replayable with randomized spawn points and rotating map selection between rounds.
Feel free to ask for a specific map layout, a scripting breakdown (Lua) for the timer/role-swap system, or a UI mockup next.

title: Upstream P0281 — one_vs_all
source_prompt:
Create a small playable co-op dark fantasy wave survival game for 1-5 players.

The game should have a classic old Roblox appearance made mostly from simple blocky parts, visible studs, medieval structures, dark lighting, fog, and a mysterious void atmosphere. Avoid realistic terrain and overly detailed modern assets.

The game begins in a small lobby called The Soul Highway, a dark space between realms and ruined timelines. The lobby should contain one large portal called a Crossing. When players enter the Crossing, teleport them into a ruined medieval fortress.

The playable mission should focus on fighting alongside friendly NPC soldiers rather than fighting alone.

Create five fixed player roles:

1. Officer
 The Officer uses a sword and can give nearby friendly NPC squads simple commands: Follow, Hold Position, Attack Target, and Regroup.

2. Vanguard
 The Vanguard uses a heavy melee weapon, has more health and stagger resistance, and is effective against elite enemies.

3. Medic
 The Medic uses a light melee weapon and can heal both players and friendly NPC soldiers.

4. Scout
 The Scout uses a light sword and a limited crossbow. Give the Scout a simple short-range grappling hook for reaching rooftops and marking incoming enemies.

5. Engineer
 The Engineer uses a hammer and can repair barricades and the fortress gate.

Allow players to select a role before entering the portal. If fewer than five players are present, the remaining roles can be represented by simple AI companions or left unused if companion AI is too complex.

The combat should be mostly medieval melee combat using swords, shields, spears, and heavy weapons. Ranged weapons should be limited. Create basic light attacks, blocking, health, enemy damage, and simple hit reactions. Prioritise working gameplay over advanced animations.

Friendly NPC soldiers should spawn in small squads. They should follow their squad leader, attack enemies, defend the objective, and retreat toward the fortress when badly overwhelmed. They should feel useful and help players hold the battlefield.

The mission structure should be:

- Players and friendly NPC soldiers defend the outer courtyard.
- Enemy waves attack the fortress.
- The Engineer must repair the damaged main gate while the others protect them.
- The Officer can position friendly NPC squads around the courtyard.
- Later waves introduce one larger elite enemy.
- After the gate is repaired, a stronger wave breaches another entrance.
- Players and surviving NPC soldiers must retreat into the inner keep.
- The final objective is to survive inside the keep for a limited amount of time.

Add a simple downed state. A downed player can be revived by the Medic. If they are not revived, respawn them during the next wave.

Use a minimal interface showing:

- Current objective
- Current wave
- Player health
- Selected role
- Number of surviving friendly NPC soldiers
- Repair progress when near the gate

At the end, show whether the fortress survived and how many friendly NPC soldiers remained.

Use placeholder blocky characters, simple scripts, and basic animations. Do not create complicated progression, shops, currencies, long cutscenes, or realistic graphics yet. This is only a gameplay concept prototype that will later have its combat and NPC systems replaced with custom systems.

title: Upstream P0285 — open_world_action
source_prompt:
I want to build an airship combat game.

# Setting:
Steampunk-styled feudal universe where humanity lives in the clouds and gets around by airship. The justification is that in this universe the atmosphere is denser so airships have an easier time floating. The game takes place in a war being fought between two major kingdoms. The player is a small fiefdom with a battle airship that may be called upon to go to battle in service of their kingdom (analogous to how knights owned castles and were called up in medieval times). The details and lore can be fleshed out after the mechanics are, but this sets the motivation for the gameplay loop

# Gameplay:
The gameplay revolves around large PvE battles in a similar style to helldivers 2. Once matchmaking selects a team of players, there is first a planning phase where the players are all debriefed with "intelligence" relating to what they're up against and where they're fighting (e.g. environmental hazards, cloud/weather cover, force composition, wildlife hazards) and can collaboratively draw up a battle plan. Then the battle begins, and depending on the objective runs to completion. After the battle, the player earns research points and money to research and buy components. They can then build/upgrade their airship and take it to combat

# Main features and open questions:
 ⁃ Damage model: I want this to be dynamic, similar to how war thunder works. For example, if you hit an ammo locker and penetrate, it should really destroy some components. Similarly, if you hit the air bag of a ship, it should start to very slowly lose lift. Naturally everyone is going to be shooting for the air bags because of this, but as in real life the egress of lift gas is very low and in this game unlike in real life it isn't flammable. You'd have to really get shredded or rammed for it to start to be a rapid issue
 ⁃ Combat Styles:
 ⁃ Classic: Similar to how ship combat is set up in world of warships or the war thunder Bluewater navies mode, but in 3d. 
 ⁃ Team: Similar to how ship combat is in sea of thieves
 ⁃ Game Modes:
 ⁃ PvP (Skirmish): Classic pvp with a ticket system, following the war thunder arcade mode formula. This mode will filter out the players that don't care about the team tactics/strategic element of the game. These battles do not affect the "world state"
 ⁃ PvE (War): Similar in idea to helldivers 2 battles, which are PvE and the outcome of which impacts the overall state of the world, and starwars battlefront's multi-stage battles where the objectives change over time. My idea is that at the start of the battle the players get debriefed and can collaborate on a rough battle plan. I'm not sure the most fun way to implement this, so some research is required as to examples of similar mechanics in other games and how they have been received. For example, what is the best way to allow visual collaboration? I imagine we need both the ability to draw up attack/defense plans, and to group players on the same team by objective (e.g. you two go attack their left flank, then during the battle the LLM orchestrating the execution of the plan presents the corresponding objective to those two players). Once the battle begins the players see objectives based on the plan selected, which should change dynamically as combat progresses. I imagine that it would be neat to create an API/MCP for setting the dynamic objectives, and using two LMaaS agents (one for the player team and one for the enemy team) to act as strategic commanders and issue battle directives. If the battle is starting to really degrade I think the remaining players should have the option to go to the "situation room" and see a similar briefing screen to what they saw before, come up with a revised plan, and then resume control of their ships with the updated objectives. 
 ⁃ Game mode combinations: Each game mode can be paired with each combat style. For example, you can do Classic War, Team War, Classic Skirmish, and Team Skirmish. Choosing classic vs team basically just switches whether your squamates control their own airships or if you work together to man one airship chosen from the library of configurations of anyone in the squad
 ⁃ Ship building: I want there to be a very diverse load out of forces you can control. We start off with a tech tree that allows basic airship design with different tradeoffs for armor firepower speed etc. But I want users to also be able to go different routes based on what they want to build, like a big glass cannon ship or a large mothership or even a small fleet of individual little airships that, in "Classic" mode would be controlled similar to how you control troops in games like mount and blade war band (you are in charge of one ship, and give general deployment commands to the others). In "Team" mode, you would all be controlling individual stations
 ⁃ Matchmaking and team comp: This is a big open question. Depending on how the shipbuilding and damage system is implemented, it will be essential to construct teams of an appropriate size for fun combat with a team composition that lends itself to interesting strategy being possible. I think that, based on the attributes of a player's deployed force (single ship or multi-ship) there should be a set of derived statistics about the ship. Then, for matchmaking, we can use an agent to search through the list of queued players and assemble a team. 
 ⁃ Procedural battle generation: Based on some set of rules, the system should procedurally generate a map consisting of obstacles, weather, wildlife hazards, etc. Then, in PvE mode, based on the selected human player team, assemble a commensurate opposing force to make the battle difficult but not impossible to win.

So to summarize, we need to flesh out the following design choices:
 ⁃ Tactical system in pve: how should the plan creation mechanic work, and how should the LLM game masters manage providing players with objectives and moving the game along in a fun way.
 ⁃ Ship driving: how should we handle the ships moving? What motion model balances the fun of high speed with the impact of seeing a capital ship slowly looming on the horizon. How does weather impact this (e.g. strong winds, lightning strikes, rain etc)
 ⁃ Ship ranking: What statistics should we track for ship builds and how should we derive them from a particular build? Based on these statistics, how can we rank vehicles with similar play styles but different components in terms of capability to provide a sense of progression that your ship gets better over time?
 ⁃ Matchmaking: Based on those statistics, what makes a fair team? How can the LLM generate it
 ⁃ Matchmaking speed: Lots of procedural generation goes into each game. How can we decouple the matchmaking queue from the world generation queue? Players should only ever be waiting to be paired with teammates, NOT for their world to be generated AFTER they are paired
 ⁃ Research and money system: How do we determine how much money and research points to assign after battle?
 ⁃ World state: How can we best emulate the engaging world-scale war aspect of helldivers 2? How much should the outcome of 1 battle impact that?
 ⁃ Monetization: How do we make money from this game? Premium components?
 ⁃ Damage system: Obviously we are basing this on war thunder, but transferring that to airships requires some refining
 ⁃ Team mode: Sea of thieves style gameplay is definitely a goal here, but that means that everything about combat has to work for both 3rd person whole ship control and an individual player running around on deck managing guns. This means we need to design all of the systems like gun control, fires, damage model and its impact on ship handling, etc in a way that is the same (uses the same code) for both game modes, just that in team mode individual players are actually within the model and running around and controlling individual components and in classic mode those same individual elements are controlled by a harness that sits on top of the system and exposes simplified controls that lets one person do everything.
 ⁃ Ship building: what are the rules about what is a valid vehicle? I think we can take inspiration from crossout's car building mechanics; the developers of that game also built war thunder and by definition have already figured out the pitfalls of allowing players to build their own vehicles

And come up with specifics for the initial set of elements in the following parts of the game that will then be expanded over time:
 ⁃ Ship parts: what does the initial tech tree look like? What are the categories? What weapons do we start off with
 ⁃ Map elements: clouds, floating rocks and cities, larger floating islands, along with team base for repair
 ⁃ Enemy types: Instead of procedurally generating enemies, it is probably easier to balance a game where we just pre-make a catalog of enemies that can be scaled in attributes or unlock at certain levels and combined to form the enemy team. It will also be faster at matchmaking time
 ⁃ Assets: I'm thinking we should use this asset pack and try to use ModelGen/PrimGen to make similar looking assets: https://kitbash3d.com/products/city-in-the-sky. We can also use these floating island assets as the substrate from which we can procedurally generate the battle maps.
 ⁃ Game lore: I want to flesh the backstory of the world out a little bit.

Future mechanics for the roadmap: 
 ⁃ Ship boarding

title: Upstream P0288 — open_world_action
source_prompt:
Here is a full breakdown of how a 3D open-world (free-roam) Police vs. Robber game operates across its core mechanics, gameplay loops, world design, and progression systems.
1. Core Architecture: Asymmetric Sandbox Design
At its core, a 3D open-world Police vs. Robber game is built on asymmetric multiplayer dynamics. Unlike traditional shooters where both teams share identical goals, this genre pits two teams with fundamentally different win conditions, toolsets, and movement rhythms against each other across a continuous 3D city.
 * Robbers (Offensive & Proactive): Win by earning money through high-stakes heists, evading capture, and converting "dirty" loot into permanent progression rewards.
 * Police (Defensive & Reactive): Win by intercepting active crimes, arresting wanted suspects, protecting urban infrastructure, and earning bounty payouts.
2. Dual Gameplay Loops
The Robber Loop: Heist, Escape, Cleanse
 * Preparation & Loadout: Robbers assemble at hidden safehouses or player-owned apartments. They equip tools tailored to their role (e.g., thermal drills, hacker tablets, C4 charges, lockpicks, or signal jammers) and select getaway vehicles.
 * Infiltration & Execution: Players travel across the 3D map to targets ranging from low-tier convenience stores to high-tier targets like central bank vaults, armored transport trucks, or jewelry stores. Executing a heist involves interactive mini-games (e.g., circuit cracking, safe tumbling, hacking security feeds) while fending off local security guards or alarm triggers.
 * The Pursuit & Laundering: Once loot is secured, a citywide alarm alerts police forces. Robbers must navigate traffic, break line-of-sight, utilize alleyways, or deploy countermeasures (smoke screens, spike-strips, signal jammers). Stolen cash is carried as "dirty money" in duffel bags, which drops if the player is downed. To spend it, robbers must reach "Fence" NPCs or safehouses to launder the cash into spendable currency.
The Police Loop: Patrol, Intercept, Incarcerate
 * Patrol & Intelligence: Officers roam the map or wait at precincts. They monitor the 3D map radar for silent alarm pings, gunfire audio signatures, and automated traffic camera alerts triggered by wanted criminals.
 * Containment & High-Speed Pursuit: Upon responding to a crime, officers coordinate perimeter lockdowns. Pursuit mechanics rely on high-speed driving physics, PIT maneuvers (Precision Immobilization Technique), spike strip deployment, and helicopter spotlight tracking.
 * Subjugation & Arrest: Unlike pure deathmatch games, police are incentivized to arrest rather than kill. Using non-lethal equipment (tasers, beanbag shotguns, tear gas, or handcuffs), officers incapacitate criminals. Successfully handcuffing a robber sends them to the city prison complex and claims the criminal's accumulated bounty.
3. Open-World Map Design
The 3D world must be engineered to support high-speed vehicular chases and intricate on-foot combat:
| Map Zone | Purpose | Features & Dynamics |
|---|---|---|
| Financial & Downtown District | High-Value Heists | Skyscrapers, bank vaults, narrow alleys, tight grid streets favoring nimble sports cars. |
| Industrial / Docks Area | Smuggling & Laundering | Shipping containers for sightline obstruction, warehouses, water access for jet skis/boats. |
| Suburban / Residential Zone | Low-Risk Crime & Hiding | Open roads, garage hiding spots, convenience stores for fast cash. |
| Prison Complex | Detainment & Jailbreaks | High-security perimeter where arrested robbers serve timed sentences or orchestrate breakouts. |
Dynamic map elements-such as interactive drawbridges, hackable traffic lights, destructible roadblocks, subway tunnels, and sewer networks-provide tactical depth during pursuits.
4. Economy, Bounty, and Progression
The game's economy creates an escalating risk-versus-reward tension through a Dynamic Bounty System:
 * Wanted Rating & Bounty Scaling: Every crime a robber commits adds to their active bounty. A small store robbery might add $1,000, while a bank heist adds $50,000.
 * Risk vs. Reward: Higher bounties make robbers a top-priority target on police radar displays, but surviving longer with a massive bounty multiplies the final payout when successfully laundered.
 * Police Payouts: Officers receive a direct percentage of the criminal's bounty upon making a successful arrest, incentivizing them to hunt high-value players rather than low-level offenders.
 * Customization & Upgrades:
 * Vehicles: Tuned engines, armor plating, run-flat tires, EMP launchers, or stealth coating.
 * Weapons & Gadgets: Silenced weaponry, drone recon tools, ziplines, grapple guns, and tactical body armor.
5. Technical & Asymmetry Balancing
To keep matches fair without making both sides feel identical, balancing relies on spatial mechanics:
 * Initiative vs. Information: Robbers hold the element of surprise by choosing when and where to strike. Once the alarm trips, police gain access to GPS tracking pings that update every few seconds.
 * Lethal vs. Non-Lethal Rewards: Police earn significantly higher XP and monetary rewards for non-lethal arrests compared to lethal kills.
 * Prison Mini-Game: When robbers are jailed, they aren't forced into a blank loading screen. They can complete prison labor tasks to reduce their sentence timer, purchase contraband from inside, or coordinate an external breakout raid with surviving crew members outside.

title: Upstream P0292 — open_world_action
source_prompt:
Let's create a single-player version of "Laser Grid Survival" where the user plays against AI bots.

Game Setup:
When the game starts, automatically spawn 30 AI-controlled humanoid bots into the lobby alongside the main player. Give the bots basic pathfinding scripts so they run forward toward the objective during the safe phases, but make them occasionally make mistakes and fail so the player has competition.

Game 1: Motion Sensor Rush
Build a long metallic hallway with a pulsing laser core computer at the end. Every few seconds, a glowing grid line sweeps the hallway.
- When the line is BLUE, the player and the AI bots sprint forward.
- When the line turns RED, an alarm blares. The player and the AI bots must freeze. Write a script for the AI bots so that 15% of them randomly fail to stop moving in time. Any player or bot that moves during the RED phase gets zapped by a laser and eliminated.

Game 2: Gravity Fractures
A high-tech chasm crossed by pairs of neon steps (one solid, one a fake holographic illusion). Write a script for the remaining AI bots so they take turns guessing which step to step on. If a bot guesses wrong, it falls and is eliminated, clearing the path or showing the player which way is safe.

Visual Style:
A gritty, sci-fi cyber-bunker. The player and bots wear simple metallic suits. Hostile NPCs are hovering security drones.

title: Upstream P0293 — open_world_action
source_prompt:
Create a fast-paced Cyberpunk movement game with custom mobile screen UI buttons arranged compactly around the standard Jump button. Add 4 specialized skill buttons: 
1. "Sandevistan": Slows down global time by 70% for 5 seconds when pressed. Give the player a 2x speed boost during this time, apply a neon-blue screen vignette effect, and emit a trail of fading holographic after-images behind the player's avatar. 10-second cooldown.
2. "Dash": Instantly propels the player 15 studs forward in the direction they are facing with a neon streak particle effect. 2-second cooldown.
3. "Slide": Triggers a low-profile sliding animation if the player is running, increasing speed briefly and lowering their physics hitbox.
4. "Grapple": Shoots a glowing neon cable toward aimed surfaces or building ledges, pulling the player smoothly to the target destination.

Generate a massive, vertical Cyberpunk city map. Fill it with towering, futuristic skyscrapers, glowing neon billboards, dark rainy streets, and elevated highway platforms. Ensure all buildings have accessible ledges, rooftops, and neon pipes perfectly spaced out so the player can seamlessly chain together the Sandevistan, Dash, Slide, and Grappling Hook mechanics to navigate across the rooftops.

title: Upstream P0294 — open_world_action
source_prompt:
Create a complete, cross-platform Cyberpunk Vector Superpower game that is fully compatible with Mobile, PC, and Console.

1. INPUT WRAPPER SYSTEM (Cross-Platform mapping):
- Map Skill 1 (Tectonic Rip) to: Mobile On-Screen Button / PC Key [E] / Console [ButtonX / X].
- Map Skill 2 (Momentum Steal) to: Mobile On-Screen Button / PC Key [Q] / Console [ButtonY / Triangle].
- Map Skill 3 (Friction Zero) to: Mobile On-Screen Button / PC Key [LeftShift] / Console [LeftTrigger / L2].
- Map Skill 4 (Gravity Flip) to: Mobile On-Screen Button / PC Key [R] / Console [RightTrigger / R2].
- Map Movement Skill (Slide) to: Mobile On-Screen Button / PC Key [C] / Console [RightStickClick / R3].
- Arrange all custom mobile buttons compactly in an ergonomic arc around the default Jump button.

2. ADVANCED POWERS & PHYSICS BACKEND:
- "Tectonic Rip": Raycast down. Instance a 12x12x2 stud asphalt part welded to the player's front as a shield. Second press: Unweld and apply a LinearVelocity of 250 studs/sec forward. Use .Touched to deal 100 damage and shatter obstacles.
- "Momentum Steal & Fling": Fire a 100-stud touch/mouse Raycast. If it hits an unanchored Part, store its AssemblyLinearVelocity into a 'StoredVelocity' variable, set the target's velocity to zero, and increase a visual 'Vector Battery' UI bar. Tapping again releases the force into a massive 50-stud radius radial shockwave punch.
- "Friction Zero": When toggled, alter CustomPhysicalProperties of feet/root parts to Friction = 0 and FrictionWeight = 100. Emit neon beam particles from heels. Let the player slide endlessly and maintain forward momentum up slanted skyscraper walls.
- "Gravitational Vector Flip": Fire a targeting beam. Clear the hit object's global gravity and apply an internal VectorForce constraint pointing 180 degrees opposite of Workspace.Gravity to violently launch it into the sky.

3. CROSS-PLATFORM MOVEMENT CODE:
- Air Dash Vector Correction: On air dash, instantly set falling Y-velocity to 0 right before applying the forward horizontal LinearVelocity thrust.
- Directional Slide: Lower Humanoid.HipHeight by 50%, trigger a slide animation, and apply a 0.5-second physics impulse of 45 studs/sec in the camera's face direction. Emit spark particles.
- Multi-Surface Wall Running: Raycast 3 studs left/right in mid-air. If a skyscraper wall is detected, disable gravity, lock Y-axis height, and apply forward velocity along the wall surface vector. Space/Jump button cancels it into a horizontal outward leap force.
- Kinetic Retention: Gradually decay high-speed velocity states over 2 seconds rather than snapping instantly to default walk speed.

4. THE MAP ENVIRONMENT:
- Generate a massive, vertical Cyberpunk concrete metropolis at night with heavy rain particle effects and wet, highly reflective rooftop surfaces.
- Fill the city with unanchored, physics-active traffic cars, loose street elements, glowing neon billboards, and grindable neon pipes connecting the buildings.

title: Upstream P0295 — open_world_action
source_prompt:
RAM VS RAVANA: THE BATTLE OF LANKA

Roblox Game Design Prompt

 

MASTER PROMPT (paste into Roblox Studio's AI / Creator Hub tool):

 

Build a Roblox action-adventure game inspired by the Ramayana epic, styled visually like a modern Indian mythological epic film. The protagonist is Lord Ram, a calm, dignified warrior-sage dressed in flowing saffron/orange robes with a simple wooden bow and a quiver of glowing golden arrows. The antagonist is Ravana, the ten-headed demon king, who rides a giant flying lotus/chariot (Pushpaka Vimana) through the skies above Lanka. The player controls Ram in a bow-and-arrow combat game where precision, patience, and dharma (righteousness) matter as much as damage output.

 

1. CORE PREMISE AND TONE

- Setting: The final battle of Lanka, from Ram's landing on the shore to the defeat of Ravana.

- Tone: Respectful, heroic, and family-friendly, closer to an epic adventure film than a violent shooter. No gore; hits are represented with light/energy VFX (golden sparks, dissolving shadow particles) rather than blood.

- Win condition frames the story correctly: Ram doesn't seek to "kill for power," he restores dharma by defeating Ravana's tyranny and rescuing Sita.

 

2. PROTAGONIST: LORD RAM

- Appearance: Saffron/ochre dhoti-style robe, simple sandals, a calm composed facial expression, hair tied back, a small tilak mark on the forehead. No aggressive posturing, idle animation shows him standing serenely, bow lowered, occasionally looking skyward with folded hands (namaste gesture) between waves.

- Weapon: A single divine bow ("Kodanda") with an infinite regular arrow supply, no ammo anxiety, this is about aim and timing, not resource management.

- Movement: Measured, grounded movement speed; a short dash/side-step ("dharmic step") to dodge incoming projectiles, rather than a frantic double-jump shooter feel.

- Voice/Flavor lines: Occasional short, calm lines when landing hits or leveling up ("Dharma prevails," "Peace through strength," "Return to light"), text captions rather than full voice acting to keep scope manageable.

 

3. ANTAGONIST: RAVANA

- Health Pool: 100,000 HP total, displayed as a large boss health bar with 10 segments (one per head), each segment depletes and a head visually "dims" as that chunk of HP is cleared, giving visual feedback on progress.

- Mount: Flying Pushpaka Vimana (lotus-chariot) that weaves across a wide arena sky in patterned flight paths (figure-8s, dive-bombs, hover-and-strike), forcing Ram to track a moving target rather than shoot a stationary boss.

- Attack Patterns (phase-based, tied to HP thresholds):

 Phase 1 (100k to 75k HP): Slow figure-8 flight, lobs fireballs Ram must dodge or shoot down.

 Phase 2 (75k to 50k HP): Summons Rakshasa pawns to swarm the arena.

 Phase 3 (50k to 25k HP): Ravana dive-bombs directly at Ram, requiring a well-timed dodge plus counter-shot to a glowing weak point for bonus damage.

 Phase 4 (25k to 0 HP): All ten heads become active simultaneously, each firing different projectile types; the arena also gets red mist reducing visibility, raising tension for the finale.

- Defeat sequence: Not a gory execution, a final "Brahmastra" arrow (unlocked only in Phase 4) strikes Ravana, all ten heads dim, the Vimana crashes gently off-screen, and a light/dharma VFX washes over the arena as Sita is freed. Ends on a hopeful, restorative note rather than a kill-shot close-up.

 

4. DAMAGE AND SCORING SYSTEM

- Standard arrow hit on Ravana: -1 HP

- Rakshasa pawn (basic minion): 1 HP, one-shot kill

- Small power-up pickup: +10 damage on next arrow

- Medium power-up pickup: +100 damage on next arrow

- Large power-up pickup: +1,000 damage on next arrow

- Rare "Brahmastra shard" pickup: +10,000 damage, limited to 3 per match

- Weak-point critical hit (glowing head during dive-bomb): x5 multiplier on current arrow

 

Power-ups spawn as glowing collectible orbs (lotus petals, sacred flames, or small idols of Hanuman) that float into the arena periodically. Collecting them charges Ram's next arrow rather than firing an automatic blast, so players must choose when to "cash in" a boosted shot for maximum value (for example, saving a 10,000-point arrow for a weak-point window).

 

A combo/focus meter rewards consecutive hits without taking damage, slowly charging toward a temporary "Divine Aim" state (slow-motion aiming, auto-highlighted weak points).

 

5. RAVANA'S FORCES: RAKSHASA PAWNS

- Small demon soldiers (1 HP each) that spawn in waves from Phase 2 onward, rushing toward Ram or firing weak projectiles.

- Visually distinct from Ravana, smaller, grey/purple-skinned, simple mace or dagger, so players instantly recognize the power gap between mook and boss.

- Killing pawns quickly (within a time window) can drop bonus power-up orbs, encouraging players to clear adds rather than ignore them.

- Optional touch: a friendly Vanara (monkey warrior) ally squad, inspired by Hanuman's army, that auto-fights pawns in the background, reinforcing the "good vs. evil, allies vs. tyranny" narrative without adding player micromanagement.

 

6. ARENA AND LEVEL DESIGN

- Act 1, The Shores of Lanka: Tutorial area teaching aim, dash, and basic pawn combat. Calm ocean/beach backdrop, golden hour lighting.

- Act 2, The Golden Gates: Mid-difficulty gauntlet with more pawns, first taste of Ravana flying overhead and taunting (non-damaging preview of Phase 1 patterns).

- Act 3, Sky Arena over Lanka Palace: The main boss fight, an open rooftop/sky platform with the palace towers below, storm clouds gathering as the fight escalates through the four phases.

- Environmental storytelling: banners, statues of Hanuman, and glowing "dharma shrines" scattered around the arena that Ram can stand near to get a small temporary shield, tying mechanics back to the mythological theme instead of generic game clutter.

 

7. UI/UX

- Boss health bar styled like an ornate temple carving, subdividing into 10 head-segments.

- Player HUD: minimalist, a small bow-charge indicator (shows if a power-up is "loaded" for the next shot), a focus/combo meter, and a compass arrow pointing toward Ravana's current position when he's off-screen.

- Victory screen: warm and celebratory, fireworks styled as diyas (lamps), a short "Lanka is free" message, Sita's silhouette reunited with Ram, rather than a generic "YOU WIN" screen.

 

8. AUDIO DIRECTION

- Instrumentation: bansuri (flute), tabla, and orchestral strings for calm exploration; escalating percussion and choir swells during boss phases.

- Hit sounds: a soft "twang plus chime" for arrows rather than harsh gunfire-style effects, keeping tone consistent with Ram's serene characterization.

 

9. PROGRESSION AND REPLAYABILITY

- Difficulty tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold Bow) that scale Ravana's HP and pawn density for players who want a harder challenge after their first clear.

- Leaderboard for fastest Ravana defeat time and highest combo streak.

- Unlockable cosmetic bow skins (sandalwood, gold-inlaid, celestial) as completion rewards, no pay-to-win power creep.

 

10. DESIGN PRINCIPLES TO KEEP IN MIND

- Respect the source material: this is a beloved epic for millions of players, keep Ram's characterization noble and composed, avoid trivializing or "video-game-ifying" his character into a generic shooter avatar.

- Non-graphic combat: light/energy-based hit effects, no blood or dismemberment, appropriate for Roblox's general audience and younger players.

- Skill over grind: power-ups reward smart timing and aim, not repetitive farming.

- Clear readability: 100,000 HP is a huge number, always show it as segmented percentages/head-icons so players get constant visual feedback on progress, not just a shrinking bar that feels endless.

 

QUICK-COPY VERSION (short form for Studio's prompt box):

 

Create a Roblox boss-battle game inspired by the Ramayana. Protagonist: Lord Ram, calm and dignified, saffron robes, wields an infinite-ammo divine bow, dash-dodge movement. Antagonist: Ravana, a ten-headed demon king with 100,000 HP (shown as 10 head-segments), riding a flying lotus chariot (Pushpaka Vimana) in patterned flight paths across a sky arena over Lanka's palace. Standard arrows deal 1 damage; collectible power-up orbs (10/100/1,000/10,000 damage) charge Ram's next shot; rare weak-point dive-bomb hits give a 5x multiplier. Ravana summons 1-HP Rakshasa pawns in waves starting mid-fight, and the battle escalates through 4 phases with more heads and projectile types active near defeat. Combat is stylized with golden light/energy VFX, no gore. Victory ends with Sita's rescue and a warm, celebratory finale, not a graphic kill.

title: Upstream P0298 — open_world_action
source_prompt:
OUTBREAK GENESIS - PROMPT 1: FOUNDATION BUILD

Create the foundation for a polished Roblox third-person co-op roguelite shooter called Outbreak Genesis.

Do not attempt to build the entire game at once. Focus on creating a stable, expandable foundation with clean scripts, organised folders, and reusable systems.

CORE GAMEPLAY

The player fights increasingly difficult waves of infected mutants inside a ruined futuristic city.

Use a third-person, over-the-shoulder camera with smooth movement and responsive combat.

The player should be able to:

- Walk and run smoothly
- Sprint
- Jump
- Dodge roll in the movement direction
- Manually aim using a crosshair
- Shoot toward the crosshair
- Reload their weapon
- Take damage and die
- Play comfortably on PC, mobile, and controller

The camera should remain behind the player and shift slightly over the right shoulder while aiming.

STARTER WEAPON

Give every player a basic futuristic assault rifle.

The rifle should include:

- Automatic firing
- Visible muzzle flash
- Bullet tracer effect
- Shooting sound
- Reload animation or reload delay
- Magazine ammunition
- Reserve ammunition
- Damage falloff over long distances
- Crosshair feedback when an enemy is hit
- Red crosshair feedback when an enemy is eliminated

Use raycasting for accurate shooting.

ENEMY SYSTEM

Create one basic infected enemy called Crawler.

The Crawler should:

- Spawn from designated enemy spawn points
- Detect the nearest living player
- Chase the player using pathfinding
- Attack at close range
- Take damage from weapons
- Display a health bar
- Play a death effect
- Drop XP crystals when defeated
- Automatically despawn after death

Enemies should be controlled by the server to reduce exploits.

WAVE SYSTEM

Create a basic wave manager.

Requirements:

- Begin Wave 1 after a short countdown
- Spawn a set number of Crawlers
- Increase the number and health of enemies each wave
- Detect when all enemies have been defeated
- Display the current wave number
- Provide a short break between waves
- Start the next wave automatically
- End the match when every player is dead

For this first build, support at least 10 waves.

XP AND LEVEL-UP SYSTEM

Defeated enemies should drop glowing XP crystals.

When a player moves close to a crystal, it should fly toward them and be collected.

Add:

- XP bar
- Player level
- Increasing XP requirements
- A level-up effect
- A temporary pause or protected state during upgrade selection

Whenever the player levels up, display three randomly selected upgrades.

The player chooses one upgrade, and the other two disappear.

Starter upgrades should include:

- Increased weapon damage
- Increased fire rate
- Increased magazine size
- Faster reload speed
- Increased movement speed
- Increased maximum health
- Health regeneration
- Additional projectile
- Critical-hit chance

Upgrades should stack and visibly affect gameplay.

USER INTERFACE

Create a clean sci-fi HUD displaying:

- Health bar
- XP bar
- Current level
- Current wave
- Remaining enemies
- Magazine and reserve ammunition
- Crosshair
- Sprint indicator or stamina bar
- Three-card upgrade selection screen

Keep the interface readable on mobile devices.

TEST MAP

Create a small ruined-city test arena containing:

- Broken roads
- Abandoned vehicles
- Damaged buildings
- Concrete barriers
- Flickering lights
- Fog or atmospheric particles
- Several enemy spawn points
- Open areas for fighting
- Obstacles enemies must navigate around

Use simple placeholder assets where necessary. Prioritise performance and gameplay functionality over detailed decoration.

TECHNICAL STRUCTURE

Organise the project using clear folders and reusable ModuleScripts.

Separate systems for:

- Player movement
- Camera
- Weapons
- Enemy AI
- Wave management
- XP and levelling
- Upgrade selection
- UI
- RemoteEvents
- Game configuration

Use server-authoritative damage, enemy spawning, XP rewards, and wave progression.

Add comments explaining important scripts.

The finished build should provide a playable prototype where players can enter the arena, fight waves of Crawlers, collect XP, level up, select upgrades, and continue until they die.

title: Upstream P0300 — open_world_action
source_prompt:
制作一款 3D 第三人称动作 Roguelike 探险游戏《深渊回响》，
使用 3D 场景、3D 角色模型和 3D 战斗表现，
镜头跟随主角背后，明确采用 3D 视角而非俯视或 2D 横版。
玩家扮演一位被困在废弃神殿地下的探险者，需要向下探索 5 层地宫，
最终击败最底层的"回响之王"逃出神殿。

【核心玩法】
· 每一层由 6～10 个 3D 房间组成，房间布局每次进入随机生成
· 房间类型包括：战斗房、宝箱房、商店房、精英怪房、休息房
· 玩家同时携带远程武器（默认魔法法杖，发射能量弹）和近战武器
 （默认短剑），可自由切换：远程用于风筝和精英怪压制，近战用于
 快速清杂兵和处决残血敌人
· 远程武器有弹药或冷却限制，鼓励与近战交替使用
· 玩家可通过跳跃、翻滚闪避敌人攻击和弹幕
· 击败敌人掉落"回响碎片"（货币）和随机符文

【成长与随机性】
· 每层结束后玩家可从 3 个随机符文中选 1 个，符文可叠加改变玩法，
 例如"每次翻滚释放冲击波""近战命中回血""射击弹返弹""连击加速"等
· 商店房可用回响碎片购买血瓶、临时增益或武器升级（远程/近战独立升级）
· 死亡后掉落所有符文，但保留少量永久强化点数用于下一局起始加强

【Boss 战】
· 第 5 层 Boss"回响之王"具有 3 阶段：召唤小怪 → 全屏弹幕 → 狂暴突进
· 击败后播放逃出神殿的结局动画

【氛围】
· 昏暗神秘的地下神殿 3D 场景，石质墙壁与火把光影，蓝紫色调
· 3D 角色带布料与武器建模，敌人为 3D 生物模型
· 背景音乐为低沉的管弦乐 + 神秘音效

title: Upstream P0304 — open_world_survival_rpg
source_prompt: Game Title: Brainrot Universe: Infinite Chaos Brainrot Universe: Infinite Chaos is a massive open-world Roblox experience where players awaken inside the mysterious Island of Brainrot, a place where every meme, trend, and chaotic internet joke has somehow become alive. Players begin with nothing except a basic "Rot Meter" that slowly fills as they explore, fight, and collect bizarre Brainrot creatures. Every Brainrot has different rarities ranging from Common, Rare, Epic, Mythic, Divine, Cosmic, and the almost impossible Reality Breaker tier. Players travel through huge themed zones including Skibidi Sewers, Sigma City, Ohio Wasteland, Rizz Resort, Grimace Forest, Banana Battlefield, AI Desert, Italian Brainrot Village, and the mysterious Glitched Void, each containing unique enemies, quests, bosses, secrets, and hidden collectibles. Players capture Brainrots by defeating them and using Rot Cubes, then level them up, evolve them, unlock powerful meme abilities, and build the ultimate squad of five Brainrots to fight alongside them. Hundreds of Brainrots exist, including Skibidi Toilet, Sigma Wolf, Gigachad, Ohio Monster, Grimace Shake, Capybara King, Baller, Tralalero Tralala, Bombardiro Crocodilo, Tung Tung Tung Sahur, Brr Brr Patapim, Cappuccino Assassino, Lirili Larila, Boneca Ambalabu, Chimpanzini Bananini, and many original creations that become increasingly ridiculous as the game progresses. Every Brainrot has unique attacks, passive skills, ultimate abilities, and evolution paths that require special items, boss drops, or hidden puzzles. Players earn Coins, Rot Crystals, Meme Essence, Chaos Tokens, and Reality Shards to purchase upgrades, cosmetics, mounts, pets, houses, and powerful equipment. The game includes massive multiplayer raids where up to 30 players battle gigantic bosses such as The King Toilet, The Sigma Emperor, The Ohio Dragon, The AI Overlord, The Brainrot Core, and the final Reality Breaker, each featuring multiple attack phases and exclusive rewards. Players complete daily quests, weekly challenges, seasonal battle passes, achievements, treasure hunts, timed world events, and random invasions where giant Brainrots appear across the map for everyone to fight together. Every few hours a Reality Rift opens, creating temporary worlds with special rules like low gravity, giant heads, backwards movement, double rewards, or random Brainrot transformations. Trading allows players to exchange Brainrots, rare items, cosmetics, and currencies while a marketplace lets creators sell custom decorations and emotes. The housing system lets players build meme mansions, decorate them with trophies, music, furniture, portals, and display their rarest Brainrots for visitors. PvP arenas include ranked leagues where players climb from Bronze to Meme God by mastering team strategy, timing abilities, and countering enemy Brainrots. Leaderboards track richest players, strongest Brainrots, fastest boss clears, highest Rot Level, rarest collections, longest streaks, and most quests completed. Hidden throughout the world are hundreds of secret caves, codes, puzzles, easter eggs, lore pages, and mysterious NPCs revealing the story that an experimental AI accidentally merged the internet with reality, causing endless Brainrot corruption that players must eventually stop. Players can unlock vehicles including meme cars, rocket shopping trolleys, giant ducks, flying pizzas, and rainbow toilets while collecting hundreds of accessories, trails, wings, particle effects, title badges, and animated emotes. Every month new Brainrots, islands, bosses, quests, cosmetics, and events are added, including holiday updates with exclusive limited rewards. The game features colourful graphics, smooth animations, funny sound effects, energetic music, satisfying progression, challenging endgame content, and constant surprises to encourage long-term play. The ultimate objective is to collect every Brainrot, defeat every boss, complete the Brainrot Index, master every ability, become the strongest Reality Breaker, and save the universe from complete meme corruption while enjoying nonstop chaotic humour, exploration, teamwork, competition, and endless replayability.

title: Upstream P0305 — open_world_survival_rpg
source_prompt:
1. Character Creation & Races:
Before spawning, display a sleek customization menu where players select their Race (choose from Aetherial, Cyber-Construct, Voidling, or Primal Humanoid), customize hair, skin tint, and aura color.
Each race grants a unique starting passive ability (e.g., faster flight, energy shield, or higher damage).
2. Starting World (Personal Realm):
Every player spawns on their own private floating sanctuary planet with floating crystal pillars, lush green fields, and pink skies, similar to a Sacred Kai Realm.
The realm features a central Portal Temple used to travel to other dimensions.
3. Multiverse Storyline & Progression:
Story: The reality fabric is decaying due to "Temporal Fractures." Players clear corrupted multiverse zones to restore balance.
Unlocks: Earning Cosmic Essence allows players to unlock 5 unique outer planets and 3 alternative Universes (Alpha, Chaos, and Omega dimensions).
4. Unique Hierarchy & Ranking System:
Include a rank hierarchy inspired by cosmic balance (without using trademarked titles):
Acolyte of Creation (Starter)
Sanctum Sentinel
Ethereal Weaver (Creation Branch) OR Void Eraser (Destruction Branch)
Cosmic Sovereign (Top Rank)
5. Controls & Mobile Ergonomics:
Make controls optimized strictly for 2-finger touch input:
Left Thumb: Virtual joystick for movement/flight.
